resources.string: Farhan settings rescue

Saves the settings of your installed Farhan to a file, so you can reinstall Farhan with a new signing key and load them back. It reads settings only, never notification or usage history. The old Farhan is stopped once when you tap Stop Farhan and export; it is not uninstalled. Force-stop may turn off its accessibility services. If you keep the old app, check and re-enable its notification and accessibility access after saving.

2. Pair this phone with itself

Open Wireless debugging, turn it on, and tap Pair device with pairing code. That dialog closes if you leave the screen, so show this app beside Settings (split screen or a floating window), then type the pairing port and the six-digit code here.

3. Check access

4. Stop Farhan and export

Before exporting, turn off notification access for the OLD Farhan in Android Settings. This helps keep its files quiet. Export stops the old Farhan once. Keep it closed until the backup is saved. Force-stop may turn off its accessibility services; check both permissions after saving if you keep the old app.

After saving, if you keep the old Farhan, check and re-enable its notification and accessibility access. Force-stop may have turned off accessibility services.

Before you uninstall Farhan:

1. If Farhan was holding notifications for you, open the old Farhan once now so it releases them.
2. In Developer options, Wireless debugging, Paired devices, remove "Farhan settings rescue".
3. Turn Wireless debugging off.

Then install the new Farhan and import this file from Settings backup.
